replay-10-seconds.context: Counterclockwise circular arrow with the number 10 in its centre. Used in video and podcast players to jump back ten seconds.

forward-30-seconds.context: Clockwise circular arrow with the number 30 in its centre. Used in video and podcast players to jump ahead thirty seconds.

start-over.context: Play triangle beside a short bar with a curved arrow arching back to the bar. Used for restarting a video, song or show from the beginning.

playback-speed.context: Speedometer arc with a needle and a small play triangle at its pivot. Used for choosing how fast audio or video plays.

ab-repeat.context: Letters A and B over a progress track with a loop arrow arching above the span between them. Used to repeat one section of a track or video.

gapless-playback.context: Five waveform bars in an unbroken row with a link bracket underneath. Used for playing tracks with no silence between them.

autoplay.context: Pill-shaped switch whose round knob holds a play triangle. Used for the setting that starts the next video or episode on its own.

play-next.context: Play triangle and a down arrow feeding into the top of a list of lines. Used to put an item first in the queue so it plays after the current one.

now-playing.context: Square album cover beside three equaliser bars of different heights. Used to show the track that is playing right now.

mini-player.context: Phone outline with a slim player bar near the bottom holding a thumbnail and a play triangle. Used for the small player that stays on screen while browsing.

sleep-timer.context: Crescent moon with a small clock face in its hollow. Used for setting audio or video to stop playing after a set time.

skip-silence.context: Two waveform bars at the sides with two chevrons squeezing a flat gap shut. Used for trimming pauses out of audio so it plays faster.

seek-bar.context: Progress track filled on the left with a round knob and a small time label above it. Used for the slider that shows and sets the playback position.

seek-preview.context: Thumbnail frame with a pointer tail above a progress bar and knob. Used for the preview picture that appears when hovering over a video timeline.

playhead.context: Vertical line topped with a downward pentagon marker crossing a row of timeline clips. Used in editors for the marker showing the current time.

video-buffering.context: Video frame with a ring of short spinner dashes, one longer than the rest. Used to show a video is loading or waiting for data.

transport-controls.context: Rounded bar holding skip back, a larger play triangle and skip forward. Used for the standard previous, play and next button group of a player.

jog-wheel.context: Large round dial with an inner platter ring and a small finger dimple. Used for the wheel on editing decks and DJ gear for scrubbing or nudging playback.

cue-point.context: Waveform bars with a vertical marker line carrying a small flag. Used to mark a spot in audio that you can jump back to.

tap-tempo.context: Fingertip pressing down on a pad with impact marks either side. Used for tapping a beat to set or detect the tempo.

frame-by-frame.context: Film frame with sprocket holes beside a step-forward triangle with a bar. Used for moving through a video one frame at a time.

frame-rate.context: Film frame with the number 60 inside and three speed lines trailing behind. Used for choosing or showing frames per second.

resume-playback.context: Video thumbnail with a play triangle and a part-filled progress bar along its bottom edge. Used for continuing something you left unfinished.
keywords: pick up where you left off

episode-list.context: Three rows each with a small play disc on the left and two text lines. Used for the list of episodes in a series or season.

scene-selection.context: Two by two grid of numbered thumbnails. Used for the menu of scenes or chapters on a disc or streaming title.

commentary-track.context: Director's chair below a speech bubble holding sound bars. Used for the extra audio track where the makers talk over a film.

audio-language.context: Speech bubble holding a waveform beside the letter A and a foreign-style glyph. Used for choosing the spoken language of a video's audio track.

translated-subtitles.context: Screen with two subtitle bars at the bottom and a small globe in the top corner. Used for choosing subtitles in another language.

skip-ad.context: Rounded button holding the letters AD and a skip-forward symbol. Used for the control that skips an advert in a video.

media-library.context: Stack of cards with the front one showing a play triangle. Used for a saved collection of videos or shows.

video-playlist.context: Video frame with a play triangle on the left and three list lines on the right. Used for an ordered list of videos to play in turn.

video-wall.context: Three by three grid of touching screens forming one large display with a play triangle in the middle. Used for tiled screen walls in control rooms and signage.

multi-view.context: Two by two grid of rounded rectangles each holding a small play triangle. Used for watching several streams at the same time.

instant-replay.context: Television with a circular replay arrow around a play triangle on its screen. Used for replaying a moment of a live broadcast or game.

highlight-reel.context: Film strip with a four-point sparkle star on its centre frame. Used for a short edit of the best moments of a game or event.

screen-mirroring.context: Television with a play triangle and a small phone below with an arrow pointing up to the screen. Used for showing a phone's display on a larger screen.

multiroom-audio.context: House outline split into two rooms with a small speaker in each. Used for playing music through speakers in several rooms.

smartphone-remote.context: Phone showing a round directional pad with a play button, with signal arcs above it. Used for a phone app that works as a remote control.

curved-tv.context: Wide television seen from the front with gently curved top and bottom edges on a short stand. Used for curved screens, monitors and home cinema displays.

eject.context: Upward pointing triangle above a flat horizontal bar. Used to eject a disc, open a tray or safely remove a drive.

eight-track-cartridge.context: Rectangular tape cartridge with a rounded back corner, a label area and an exposed tape slot. Used for retro audio formats and nostalgic music themes.

in-flight-entertainment.context: Back of an airplane seat with a small screen showing a play triangle and a headphone jack below it. Used for seatback screens and movies on flights.

rec-indicator.context: Camera viewfinder corner brackets with a large filled dot and the letters REC at the top. Used to show that a camera is recording.

tally-light.context: Small box camera with a round lamp on top and short rays around the lamp showing it is live. Used for the light that shows which camera is on air.

bass-boost.context: Speaker with a large low sound wave and a small up arrow beside it. Used for turning up the low frequencies in audio.

noise-cancellation.context: Headphones with a wave entering one cup and flattening to a straight line. Used for the mode that blocks outside noise.

transparency-mode.context: Headphones with sound arcs passing between the ear cups toward the centre. Used for the mode that lets outside sound through.

mono-audio.context: Single speaker cabinet with a woofer and tweeter above the letter M. Used for the setting that plays the same sound from one channel.

stereo-audio.context: Two speaker cabinets side by side above the letters L and R. Used for left and right channel sound.

audio-output.context: Speaker and headphones side by side with a curved arrow arching from one to the other. Used for switching where sound is played.

lossless-audio.context: Smooth unbroken waveform curve inside a diamond outline. Used to mark high quality audio that keeps every detail of the source.

hdr-video.context: Rounded badge with a half-filled sun above the letters HDR. Used to mark video with high dynamic range.

8k-resolution.context: Rounded badge containing the bold characters 8K. Used to mark very high resolution video.

sd-video.context: Rounded badge containing the bold characters SD. Used to mark standard definition video.

audio-visualizer.context: Small circle ringed by short radiating bars of varying length like a radial spectrum. Used for animated displays that react to sound.

echo-effect.context: Sound wave arc followed by two smaller fading copies stepping away to the right. Used for delay and echo audio effects.

reverb-effect.context: Speaker inside a room outline with sound waves bouncing off the walls. Used for reverb and room sound effects.

distortion-effect.context: Waveform whose peaks are sliced flat at a top and bottom line like a clipped signal. Used for distortion, overdrive and clipping.

pitch-shift.context: Music note with a small up arrow and a small down arrow stacked beside it. Used for raising or lowering pitch.

time-stretch.context: Waveform block with outward pointing arrows at both ends pulling it longer. Used for changing the length of audio without changing its pitch.

audio-compressor.context: Tall waveform squeezed between two horizontal bars with inward arrows. Used for dynamic range compression in audio mixing.

audio-fade.context: Trapezoid volume envelope rising from zero, holding level, then sloping back down, with waveform bars inside. Used for fade in and fade out edits.

audio-stems.context: Song waveform on the left branching into three separate lanes of waveform. Used for splitting a mix into separate instrument and vocal tracks.

sound-effects.context: Jagged starburst shape with a small waveform in its centre. Used for libraries and buttons of short sound effects.

lip-sync.context: Open mouth beside a waveform with a bracket underneath linking the two. Used for matching speech to mouth movement in video.

volume-limiter.context: Speaker with sound waves that stop at a solid vertical ceiling line. Used for capping the maximum volume.

show-notes.context: Document page with text lines and a small microphone in its top corner. Used for the written notes and links that go with a podcast episode.

call-in-show.context: Studio microphone on a stand beside a telephone handset. Used for radio or podcast shows that take calls from listeners.

digital-radio.context: Compact portable radio with a small text display, speaker holes and a short antenna. Used for digital audio broadcasting and portable tuners.

radio-scanner.context: Handheld receiver with a long rubber antenna, a small frequency screen and a grid of keys. Used for scanning radio frequencies.

fm-transmitter.context: Car socket plug with a round display head and radio waves rising from its top. Used for sending phone audio to a car stereo over FM.

broadcast-van.context: Van seen from the side with a satellite dish raised on its roof. Used for outside broadcasts and live news trucks.

razor-tool.context: Blade pointing down at the gap where a timeline clip has been cut in two. Used for the cut tool in video and audio editors.

in-out-points.context: Opening and closing brackets around a highlighted span on a timeline. Used for marking the start and end of the part of a clip to use.

clip-trim.context: Film clip block with thick handles at each end and a small arrow pushing one end inward. Used for shortening a clip on an editing timeline.

freeze-frame.context: Film frame with a snowflake in its centre. Used for holding a single frame of a video still.
